_README: Bulk-import template. POST/PUT this shape to /api/admin/simulations/import (staff auth required). Each entry in `simulations` becomes one simulation (upserted by `slug`) plus its prompts and one active rubric. For new simulations, omit `id` entirely — it is optional and the database assigns it. Rows are matched by `slug`. Replace every [BRACKETED] placeholder. Imported simulations land in `draft` status for reviewer signoff.

simulations.title: Threat Intelligence: Supply-Chain Compromise at [Org Name]
simulations.description: [One-line scenario summary — e.g. triage a suspected third-party software update compromise affecting a retail bank.]
simulations.brief_short: [2-3 sentence framing the candidate reads before starting. e.g. A CERT advisory reports a trojanised update from a payments vendor used by your bank.]
simulations.brief_full: [Full briefing. Describe the org, the alert source (national CERT advisory), the affected third-party component, and what the SOC has observed so far. Keep it specific but fictional — do not reference any real vendor or breach.]
simulations.video_transcript: [Optional transcript of a stakeholder video brief. Leave as empty string if there is no video.]

prompts.title: Indicator triage
prompts.question: [Given the attached CERT advisory excerpt, identify which indicators of compromise (hashes, domains, IPs) are most credible and explain how you prioritised them.]
guidance: Distinguish high-confidence atomic indicators from low-confidence ones
Note any indicators that require enrichment before action
State your confidence level and why

prompts.title: Attribution & TTP mapping
prompts.question: [Map the observed behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK techniques and assess whether attribution to a known actor is supportable from the evidence provided.]
guidance: Cite specific ATT&CK technique IDs
Separate what the evidence shows from what you are inferring
Avoid over-attribution — say so if attribution is not supportable

prompts.title: Business-risk assessment
prompts.question: [Assess the risk this compromise poses to the bank's payment operations and customer data. What is the realistic worst case?]
guidance: Tie technical impact to a concrete business outcome
State assumptions explicitly
Quantify likelihood and impact where you can

prompts.title: Containment recommendation
prompts.question: [Link to a one-page containment plan (Google Doc / Notion) recommending immediate actions for the SOC and the vendor-management team.]
guidance: Order actions by priority and feasibility
Separate immediate containment from longer-term remediation
Identify who owns each action

prompts.title: Stakeholder brief
prompts.question: [Write a 5-line executive summary for the CISO that a non-technical board member could also follow.]
guidance: Lead with the bottom line
Avoid jargon or define it inline
End with a clear ask or recommendation

rubric.systemPrompt: You are an expert Cyber Threat Intelligence assessor evaluating a candidate's response to a supply-chain compromise scenario in financial services. Score each task against its three criteria using the scoring scale. Be specific, cite evidence from the candidate's response, and never invent details the candidate did not provide. [Replace with your finalised assessor instructions.]

criteria.name: Indicator credibility
criteria.description: [Correctly separates high- vs low-confidence indicators and justifies the split.]

criteria.name: Prioritisation
criteria.description: [Prioritises indicators by actionability and risk, not volume.]

criteria.name: Confidence framing
criteria.description: [States confidence levels and the reasoning behind them.]

criteria.name: ATT&CK accuracy
criteria.description: [Maps behaviour to correct, specific ATT&CK techniques.]

criteria.name: Evidence discipline
criteria.description: [Separates observed evidence from inference; avoids over-attribution.]

criteria.name: Impact linkage
criteria.description: [Connects technical impact to a concrete business outcome.]

criteria.name: Clarity for non-technical readers
criteria.description: [Understandable to a board member; jargon defined or avoided.]

criteria.name: Actionable ask
criteria.description: [Ends with a clear recommendation or decision request.]

rubric.outputInstructions: [Optional. Return-format instructions appended to the assessor prompt, e.g. a JSON schema for per-task scores. Set to null if not used.]

simulations.title: Threat Intelligence: Ransomware Indicator Triage at [Org Name]
simulations.description: [One-line summary — e.g. assess a single ransomware indicator flagged in a CERT advisory and decide whether it warrants escalation.]
simulations.brief_short: [2-3 sentence framing. e.g. A CERT advisory lists a file hash linked to an active ransomware campaign; your manager wants a triage note.]
simulations.brief_full: [Full briefing describing the advisory, the indicator, and what your SOC tooling has and has not seen. Keep fictional.]

prompts.title: Indicator assessment
prompts.question: [Assess the single indicator from the advisory: is it actionable, and what enrichment would raise your confidence?]
guidance: State whether the indicator is atomic, computed, or behavioural
List the enrichment sources you would consult
Give a clear actionable / not-actionable verdict

prompts.title: Escalation decision
prompts.question: [Recommend whether to escalate to incident response and justify the threshold you applied.]
guidance: Make the escalation criterion explicit
Weigh cost of escalation against risk of inaction
Be decisive

prompts.title: Triage note
prompts.question: [Link to a short triage note (Google Doc / Notion) capturing the indicator, your verdict, and next steps for the on-call analyst.]
guidance: Keep it scannable
Record the decision and its rationale
List concrete next steps

criteria.name: Cost/risk balance
criteria.description: [Weighs escalation cost against risk of inaction.]

criteria.name: Scannability
criteria.description: [Note is concise and easy to scan.]
